summary: Capture bounded GitHub lifecycle history in claims and measure rolling merges and final ready cycles

replay.detail: Admitted source-sequenced capture commits publish at most four normalized fact references; staging is invisible. Corrections supersede revisions. Versioned plugin replay cursors bind finite coverage snapshots to source, generation, grant and scope.

schema.detail: Adds bounded github.fact.observed, github.capture.committed, github.capture.authority and github.capture.fenced kinds plus native github-source and effective-dated github-scope declarations. These facts are durable; operational mirror content remains disposable.

rules.detail: A selected fenced source authority acquires all authors through existing repository observers and shared HTTP budget. Unknown or incomplete history never becomes a successful objective evaluation. No default roster or throughput/latency policy is installed.

compatibility.detail: Configured plugin pull reads use canonical normalized claims with operational mirror supplements and report incomplete projection explicitly. Adds non-client-v0 replay and trusted-local owning-person authority operations. Native DSL supports GitHub rolling counts and measured-only final-ready-to-merged latency; retires the proxy merge-latency declaration.

downtime.detail: No live source is enabled by installing this change. Local capture indexes rebuild incrementally from claims; ordinary daemon restart is sufficient to load code.

manual.detail: Activation requires explicit owning-person grant admission, source selection, effective-dated scope, repository observers, private-replication admission and credential routing. Source declarations create neither observers nor grants. Transfers fence the old member before selecting a successor.

recovery.detail: Retain durable capture claims and backups. Disposable projection loss is replayable; facts staged before a failed publication stay invisible. Do not remove external ledgers until every consumer migrates. Older binaries cannot acquire the new source contract; fence acquisition before binary rollback.
